sources.claim: Diagnosing repeated container exits requires previous termination state, exit code, events and prior application logs. CrashLoopBackOff alone is a restart symptom, not a specific cause.

ImagePullBackOff indicates image pull failure with backoff; event details separate missing images from authorization and network failures. Historical pull events can be examined in Cloud Logging under the k8s_pod resource. Image pulls do not use a workload's Workload Identity Federation credentials.
k8s_pod uses project_id, location, cluster_name, namespace_name and pod_name labels. The fixture packet explicitly distinguishes supplied application and artifact records from Pod events.

a.conclusion: The image was pulled and the process started, then the application repeatedly exited with code 1 on a non-integer configuration value. This supports an application startup crash, not an image pull failure, OOM diagnosis or an unexplained cluster failure.
next_checks: The application owner traces the effective PRICE_BAND_DECIMALS setting and compares the accepted configuration contract with release 4.8.0; avoid dumping unrelated environment variables or secrets.
The release owner decides a reviewed correction and rollout after bounded validation; a restart alone does not repair the observed parse failure.
Casey asks the platform owner for later readiness and client-success observations after any approved repair, without requiring node access or kubectl from this lane.
unsupported: Calling this an image retrieval or registry authorization failure despite the successful pull/start records.
Diagnosing OOM or liveness failure merely from CrashLoopBackOff.
Deleting Pods, restarting, editing configuration, fetching cluster credentials, running kubectl or claiming recovery.
unknowns: How the invalid setting was introduced and whether other workloads share it.
Whether a corrected configuration will pass later initialization and restore sustained risk-check outcomes.

b.conclusion: The container has not started because the selected image tag is missing, corroborated by not-found events and the artifact-owner inventory. There is no application termination to diagnose in this Pod; later application behavior remains untested.
next_checks: The release/artifact owner reconciles the Deployment's exact repository/tag against the publication record and intended immutable image identity.
The platform owner can supply scoped additional event or registry-access observations if the publication evidence conflicts; no credentials or broad IAM grant is needed to interpret this packet.
Following an owner-approved correction, verify image retrieval, start, readiness and sustained request outcomes separately.
unsupported: Inventing an application configuration parse error, process exit or OOM when no container has started.
Assuming registry IAM denial or modifying Workload Identity because any image pull error means an authorization problem.
Blindly restarting, substituting an image tag, publishing an image, running kubectl or declaring that a successful pull would prove full recovery.
unknowns: Whether publication omitted the intended image or the workload selected the wrong reference.
Whether the intended image will start and serve successfully after it is made available through an approved change.
